title: The End of the Static Screen: Architecting Intent-Driven UX — Gus Iwanaga, commercetools
talk_summary: A UX/product leader at commercetools describes building an intent-driven generative UI where an orchestrator extracts intent, invokes tools, and emits a declarative UI spec that an LLM arranges into a constrained layout hierarchy. The transferable core is not the UI itself but the pattern of codifying domain knowledge into schemas, catalogs, and slot hierarchies so a non-deterministic model produces consistent, reviewable output.

takeaways.technique: Declarative spec instead of free-form model output
takeaways.what_they_do: The orchestrator emits a structured UI spec (Zod-schema-validated) that must conform to a protocol, and a renderer turns it into native components, rather than letting the LLM emit raw HTML/JSX.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the orchestrator will just broadcast this UI description. It's like a UI spec ... we use the Zod schema and then you got to be compliant

takeaways.technique: Codify domain knowledge into a constrained hierarchy
takeaways.what_they_do: They encode UX layout knowledge as layout -> slot -> sub-slot -> component-category, and map retrieved components back up that hierarchy so placement is steered rather than random.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is literally us codifying our UX knowledge into this agent ... layout to slot to sub slot to components

takeaways.technique: Catalog as contract + synthetic query generation
takeaways.what_they_do: The component catalog is treated as the contract between agent and UI, every property matters, and they generate synthetic queries to test that queries map to the right components.
An orchestrator extracts intent, locates and invokes tools/agents, then hands 'ammunition and context' to a downstream agent that produces the final artifact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the orchestrator can then just extract the intent of the query ... enough what I call ammunition and context for the UX agent

takeaways.technique: Constrain the model's freedom to reduce variance
takeaways.what_they_do: They rejected full LLM autonomy because output varied wildly across turns (Q1 vs Jan-Mar, inconsistent KPIs) and chose a middle 'declarative' path that keeps design-system compliance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't want to delegate too much of the actual experience to the LLM. You got to find alternatives
